newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond puts attract buyers.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond puts attract buyers.

text.p: Buying interest in put options on U.S. Treasury bond futures picked up as the underlying futures pushed to their lowest price in a week.
June bond futures eroded throughout the session, then ended just off their lows at 107-10.

A European banking firm bought June 105-00 puts, a Wall Street dealer firm bought the June 107-00/108-00 put spreads, a second dealer bought June 105 puts and a U.S. brokerage bought September 106-00 puts, bond floor sources said. They tied some of the activity to hedging of recently placed long positions in futures and said some of it may be speculative.
Implied volatility for at-the-money June 108-00 straddles was up slightly from the previous session, quoted at 9.30 percent late in the day versus 9.13 percent at Wednesday's close.

Bond volatilities have gradually firmed, pushing back above 9.00 percent after scraping the bottom of historical ranges earlier this month. But the relative quiet of the past week has capped the momentum, floor brokers said.
At current levels, implied volatility is roughly midway between the historic lows of 7.00-7.20 percent and highs of 11.00-11.50 percent, one broker said.
One trading firm was a seller of volatility, selling 2,000 covered June 106-00 puts delta neutral when bond futures were at 107-24.
Many options analysts expect volatility to remain supported ahead of next week's heavy slate of U.S. economic data, then probably decline again in typical fashion once the reports are past.
"I think it's getting bid up a little because of the numbers coming out," said one floor broker for a U.S. bank.
Next week's calendar includes the first-quarter employment cost index Tuesday, the National Association of Purchasing Management April index Thursday and April employment data Friday.

Implied volatilities also continued to push higher in Eurodollar options, with the September quarterly gaining 0.5 point to 11.20 percent and December 0.3 point higher at 13.00 percent. Short-dated midcurve option volatility rose to 17.20 percent in June, up 0.2 point, and was steady at 16.60 percent in September.

On the Eurodollar floor, one trading firm was noted executing a large one-by-two put spread in July options, which are priced from September futures. The firm bought 93.75 puts while selling twice the amount of 93.50 puts. The trade realizes its maximum profit if the short position expires when futures are at 93.50.
September Eurodollar futures settled Thursday at 93.68.
Floor brokers said the trade looked like a bet the Federal Reserve will conduct one 25-basis-point tightening by the fall.
